jobs.prompt:
S10 Command Center, Hive page, round 8 (Hive scored 3.8/5 against the target; goal 4.5+).
GOAL: the owner wants this page to look IDENTICAL to the target image docs/design/reference/hive-target.png in composition, components, styling and motion. OPEN AND STUDY THE TARGET IMAGE FIRST, then the current screenshots: coordination/review/cc-grade/r8/hive-desktop.png (1440x900), coordination/review/cc-grade/r8/hive-desktop-b.png (same page about 0.8 s later: if the two look the same, nothing is animating) and coordination/review/cc-grade/r8/hive-phone.png (390x844; the target has no phone view, so make a faithful single-column adaptation), and coordination/review/cc-grade/r8/hive-full.png (the whole desktop page including what is below the fold).
The target's text and numbers are illustrative. Keep the app's REAL data (project names, ticket titles, counts) and its data bindings; match everything else: layout and placement, shapes, borders, glows, gradients, colours, typography, spacing, icons, and animations.
Motion is required where the target implies it (particles and streams flowing, the ring and orbit, scan or progress motion, live chips pulsing), with CSS animations or requestAnimationFrame on canvas/SVG, smooth at 60 fps, paused under prefers-reduced-motion.
Fix every grader item below in order, then keep going toward the target until you run out of clear differences. You cannot re-render, so reason concretely about sizes at 1440x900 and 390x844 (heights vs content, grid tracks, overflow).
Never hard-code sample numbers. Empty values render as a short muted line, never a blank box.
Keep every hook other code and tests rely on: #command-center-root, .hive-shell, [data-project-id] on Hive project nodes, .cc-cockpit-shell, #cc-cockpit-main, and the stylesheet links in command-center.html (you cannot edit that file). Existing tests in your context must keep passing; update a test only where it asserted the old look, never its data behaviour.
Real browsers: never call array methods on .children/.childNodes/getElementsByTagName/getElementsByClassName/querySelectorAll results; use Array.from (tests/watch-assets-dom-collections.test.mjs enforces it).
Exactly one tasteful glitch effect in the whole app (the brand wordmark, via tools/watch-assets/cc-glitch.js, read-only). Read coordination/review/cc-design-contract.md for file ownership; if an item needs a file outside your outputs, skip it and name it in your summary.
You also own the first-visit tour (tools/watch-assets/cc-tour.js) for both pages: it never opens by itself; only the help button starts it.

GRADER ITEMS:
1. PROBLEM: Particle streams are far too faint and sparse. The target has dense, bright lane-coloured sprays bursting from every node into the ring; the app shows a few dim dots and thin curved lines, so the ring looks disconnected from the nodes.
   WHERE: Between each project card and the ring, all around the centre
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cc-hive-mount.js
   CHANGE: Raise the per-node particle budget to roughly 60-120, draw with ctx.globalCompositeOperation='lighter', radius 1-2.5px with shadowBlur 6-10px in the lane colour, emit along a bezier from the card edge to the ring with a bright comet head and a tapering trail, and add a few 3-4px bloomed sparks per stream.
2. PROBLEM: The ring is smaller, thinner and less layered than the target's. The target ring is a thick glowing band with two inner concentric rings, a dotted outer ring, radial spokes and a heavy pink bloom; the app ring is a single thin gradient stroke with a modest glow.
   WHERE: Centre of the page
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cc-hive.css
   CHANGE: Scale the ring to about 30% of viewport width (the target is ~440px at 1320px), make the main band 6-8px, add two thinner inner rings and a 1px dotted outer ring, stack glows (filter: drop-shadow(0 0 24px) and drop-shadow(0 0 60px) in pink/violet), and draw the radial spokes at ~0.15 opacity.
3. PROBLEM: The session log has no mini bar chart. The target ends the log with the command line and a coloured 'forks per second' bar chart; the app shows the command line then the note 'no completion times in the ledger' and a large empty area.
   WHERE: Bottom-left panel, below the command line
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/hive-panels.js
   CHANGE: Derive the chart from data that is present (session-log events per minute, or tickets per project coloured by status), render ~40 bars 4px wide in lane colours with a mono caption, and only show the text note when there are literally zero events.
4. PROBLEM: The right panel has no step chart. The target shows four bars, then a pink glowing step-line ('decision latency'), then two stat rows; the app has the bars and stat rows with nothing in between and empty space below.
   WHERE: Bottom-right panel, below the four status bars
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/hive-panels.js
   CHANGE: Render an SVG step-line (stroke pink 1.5px, filter drop-shadow glow) from a real series such as cumulative done counts or done-per-project percentages, with a small mono caption beneath, and keep the stat rows under it so the panel ends level with the others.
5. PROBLEM: The 'who answered' bars are missing. The target's middle panel shows three coloured bars with right-aligned values; the app's 'WHO BUILT (24 H)' section shows the note 'no per-lane job counts in the board data' instead.
   WHERE: Middle panel, below DONE PER PROJECT
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/hive-panels.js
   CHANGE: Compute the bars from a grouping that is available (tickets by worker kind, or done / in review / ready) with coloured bar fills and values in the matching colour; show the note only when no grouping exists.
6. PROBLEM: The three bottom panels are uneven. The extra nine-row DONE PER PROJECT list makes the middle panel ~700px tall while the left and right columns have large empty areas; in the target all three columns are equally dense and end on one line.
   WHERE: Bottom panel block
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/hive-panels.js
   CHANGE: Render done-per-project as a compact two-column mini list (or top N with '+n more'), move the stat rows up, and set the grid to align-items: stretch with content padding so all three columns finish at the same height.
7. PROBLEM: The header carries an extra navigation row (COMMAND CENTER / COCKPIT / CLASSIC / SEARCH / TOUR) under the counters, and the 'A run failed' toast is jammed against the header rule beside it. The target header is only wordmark, description, counters and LIVE.
   WHERE: Header, right side
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cc-hive.css
   CHANGE: Collapse the nav into a small '···' menu at the far right of the counters (or move it to the footer line), and position the toast fixed at bottom-right with a slide-in animation so it never touches the header.
8. PROBLEM: On the phone the nav row overflows and is clipped on the left ('ENTER' is all that remains of COMMAND CENTER), hiding content.
   WHERE: Phone view, below LIVE
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cc-hive.css
   CHANGE: In the max-width: 480px rule set the nav to flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: flex-start; overflow: visible with a 6px row gap, or hide it behind the same '···' menu.

COORDINATOR NOTES: the floating help button and the extra nav row are yours (cc-tour.js and the header in cc-hive-mount.js): put the nav into the single header line like the target (small mono links), make help a small header link, and move the run-failed notice into the header LIVE area. For the who-answered bars and the charts, use the snapshot fields the port added in tools/command-center-snapshot.mjs (read-only here); if a field is missing, show the chart with a muted note instead of dropping it.

GRADER ITEMS:
1. PROBLEM: The two columns are unbalanced. The target has two full columns of ten rows numbered 01-20 continuously; the app shows eight rows on the left and only three on the right (numbered 01-03 again), leaving a large empty area under the right column down to the loop strip.
   WHERE: Right ticket column
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cockpit-lists.js
   CHANGE: Build one ordered list of every ticket in the stage (running, then ready, then done), split it in half across the two columns with continuous numbering, use the ON chip for running, the play glyph for ready and the check for done; and give the column container align-content: space-between so a shorter column still spans the height.
2. PROBLEM: Counts contradict each other: the header says 5 DONE and 9 LEFT, the right column shows three done rows, the left column eight open rows, and the worker stream shows four finished tickets.
   WHERE: Header stats, ticket columns, worker stream
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cockpit-lists.js
   CHANGE: Drive the header counts, both columns and the stream from the same ticket array with no per-column cap or stage filter, and if a column must be truncated append a '+n more' row so the visible numbers still add up.
3. PROBLEM: Almost nothing moves between frames: only the orbit dot and the path pulse shift. The robot, its glow, the ON chip, the LIVE dot and the stream progress bars are static.
   WHERE: Centre robot, active row, stream cards
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cc-cockpit.css
   CHANGE: Add a 4s ease-in-out translateY(-6px) bob on the robot with the shadow ellipse scaling inversely, a slow stroke-dashoffset drift on the orbit ellipse, an opacity pulse on the ON chip and LIVE dot, and animate stream progress bars from 0 to their width on mount.
4. PROBLEM: A floating '?' help button overlaps the SWARM LOOP strip on desktop and sits on top of the 03 index chip on the phone; the target has no floating controls.
   WHERE: Bottom-left of the viewport
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cc-cockpit.css
   CHANGE: Move the help control into the breadcrumb bar beside the '···' button, or make it position: fixed; right: 16px; bottom: 16px with a high z-index and a 12px safe margin so it never covers content.
5. PROBLEM: The dotted path from the orbit to the active row is a jagged polyline with large white dots; the target uses a smooth curve with small dots and a bright node at each end.
   WHERE: Between the orbit ellipse and the active row
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cockpit-view.js
   CHANGE: Draw an SVG cubic bezier from the nearest orbit point to the row's right edge with stroke 1px rgba(255,255,255,.6), stroke-dasharray 2 6, 3px end dots, and a travelling 4px orange pulse via a stroke-dashoffset animation.
6. PROBLEM: The breadcrumb starts with a teal gradient 'SW' logo tile and ends with a '···' button; the target breadcrumb is plain mono uppercase text with no tile.
   WHERE: Top-left of the header
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cockpit-view.js
   CHANGE: Replace the tile with a mono text crumb (SWARM / THE HIVE / project) in the same letter-spacing and colour as the rest of the line, and move '···' to the end of the right-hand stats line.
7. PROBLEM: An extra RUN STREAM block sits between the worker stream and the stack, mostly empty with one card; the target goes straight from the 2x2 stream grid to the stack.
   WHERE: Below the worker stream
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cockpit-view.js
   CHANGE: Fold the orchestrator run into the worker stream grid as a card with a teal top rule, or render it as a one-line strip styled like the loop strip so the page keeps the target's vertical rhythm.
8. PROBLEM: The robot's bloom is weaker than the target's strong orange radial glow behind and beneath the sprite.
   WHERE: Centre robot
   FILE: tools/watch-assets/cc-cockpit.css
   CHANGE: Add a ::before radial-gradient (rgba(255,120,80,.35) to transparent at 60%) sized 1.6x the robot behind it, and filter: drop-shadow(0 0 30px rgba(255,110,70,.45)) on the sprite.

COORDINATOR NOTES: column balance: split the ticket list into two columns of up to ten rows each, numbered continuously (01-20) across both, ordered as the target implies (active/next on the left, done at the end), and derive every count shown on the page (header, columns, stack, worker stream) from the same ledger list so they never disagree. The floating help button is created by cc-tour.js (Hive job): do not add your own; if it overlaps your content, leave a clear note in your summary. Remove the extra RUN STREAM block (fold its one useful line into the NOW RUNNING card).
